title: Choose the visual world
question: Nixie is out; The Field Instrument joins by request. Keep the roll, take a card, or re-roll.

options.label: The Team Whiteboard
options.lineage: the hackathon war-room whiteboard: marker strokes, sticky notes, drawn grids, washi tape
options.thesis: The homepage as the team's working whiteboard: the live event drawn big in marker, projects as sticky notes, the semester sketched as a calendar strip.
materials: four marker colors with teal as the house marker
options.viewport: A crisp whiteboard: the live event blocked in black marker with a red countdown, a hand-drawn connector to a row of sticky-note projects, the semester calendar sketched along the bottom, one teal marker underline marking what matters.
options.risk: Whiteboard mess is the failure mode; refinement lives in disciplined strokes over a ruled grid, or it reads kindergarten.

options.label: HyperCard Shoebox
options.lineage: 1987 HyperCard: the home stack, buttons anyone can paint, reading and making in one object
options.thesis: The original welcoming home interface: every event a card, every action a visible button, and admin is the same tool with the lid off.
options.case: Reader/author duality maps team-operable judging exactly; the one-bit world must smuggle the teal thread without breaking.

options.label: Crisis Wall
options.lineage: 90s mecha-anime command centers: phosphor orange on black, monumental countdowns
options.thesis: The live event as an operations wall: seven-segment countdown at monumental scale, condition bars, every reading framed.
options.case: Peak ops drama and engineers adore it, but a wall of alarms is the opposite of a welcoming home.

options.label: The Field Instrument
options.lineage: Teenage Engineering OP-1 / OP-Z: pro pocket instruments, color-coded modes, geometric pictograms
options.thesis: The judging tool as a pocket instrument: a light chassis, four color-coded encoder dials, crisp small labels, dense and legible and quietly playful.
options.case: Engineers get real instrument density, students get the joyful object; fails as skeuomorph kitsch if dials decorate instead of operate.
options.viewport: The homepage as the instrument's face: the live event on a crisp dark display module, mode marked by a color-coded pictogram, four encoder dials bound to the stats, projects as a grid of square keys.
options.risk: Knob-and-dial skeuomorph kitsch if it decorates instead of operating; every dial must bind to real data or a real action.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The familiar dark judging dashboard — Devpost's world, executed impeccably in HackJudge teal.
canonCard.viewport: Dark dashboard with clean event cards, one teal accent, stats where expected; full craft, zero surprises.
